content:
Elon Musk appeared to be irritated by Jeremy Culhane’s impression of him on “Saturday Night Live” over the weekend.

The billionaire, a little under 24 hours after the comedian broke out the impression on the NBC comedy sketch show, responded to a user on his X platform who rated the performance 7/10.

Culhane — a featured player known for his impressions of Tucker Carlson and Vice President JD Vance — debuted his Musk on “Weekend Update” earlier this month after the billionaire’s preferred midterms candidates mostly flopped despite funneling hundreds of millions of dollars into their campaigns, especially in Texas.

“That’s what I call an epic, vulgar roast!” said Culhane’s Musk of host Colin Jost stressing that his record with the candidates was the reason he was making headlines.

On Saturday, Culhane broke out the impression again in the “SNL” cold open where a CIA agent (played by host John Mulaney) advises Musk and other top tech executives how to identify women who are “clearly” spies, poking fun at the scandal that led to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation.

“lol,” responded Musk in another post alongside a Venn diagram with “humor” in the left circle, “SNL” in the right circle and a small area in between with the words “the good sketches.”

Musk also responded “exactly” to a user who claimed that “politically hate bated rage started consuming” the show’s sketches, adding that insults aren’t funny whereas joke are.

“I see a rebound and wonderful new legacy for Saturday Night Live with changes that will be found, Politically economically and globally,” the user wrote. “Love will bring laughter.”

On Monday, Culhane shared a screenshot of Variety’s coverage of Musk’s review on his Instagram stories, writing in a caption taken from his “SNL” script, in a way: “Talk about an epic vulgar roast.”
